classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied acute-case proof scaffold through radius–tangent perpendicularity, equal-radius base angles and the centre–circumference theorem.

content.prompt:
Here is a different proof of the alternate segment theorem.

Let $AB$ be a chord of a circle, and let $SAT$ be the tangent at $A$.

Let $\theta=\angle BAT$ be an acute angle. We must prove that $\angle APB=\theta$.

spec.description: Acute tangent–chord proof with constructed radii OA and OB.
spec.mathematics: P lies on major arc AB; OA=OB and OA is perpendicular to the tangent.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, named points and unknowns; no calculated answers.

sizing.exceptionReason: Circle/tangent incidences and complete10pt labels determine the required width; final height and label clearance require the existing rendered review.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Join the radii $OA$ and $OB$. What is the size of $\angle BAO$?

answer.worked: $OA\perp AT$ (radius and tangent). Thus $\angle OAT=90^\circ$, so $\angle BAO=90^\circ-\theta$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the size of $\angle AOB$?

answer.worked:
The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre standing on the same arc $AB$. Thus
$$\angle APB=\frac12(2\theta)=\theta.$$
